description: Hardcoded credential: docker-compose MySQL root password in db service environment block: anyone reusing the committed file inherits a fixed root credential for the container.
Active debug code: .env.example LOCAL_WP_DEBUG=true preset: copies outside local development enable active debug code and widen the error-disclosure surface.
Debugging code exposure: .env.example LOCAL_WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY=true preset: copies outside local development render PHP errors and paths to the browser output.
Cleartext transmission: POP3 client fsockopen with no SSL/TLS or STARTTLS option: mail username, password and message bodies traverse the network unencrypted.
Cleartext transmission: wp-mail.php passes mailserver_pass to POP3 over unencrypted socket: configured mailbox password is sent cleartext on every poll.
OS command injection: Snoopy::_httpsrequest exec curl_path without escapeshellarg: writable curl_path property yields shell execution on HTTPS fetch.
Unmaintained component: Snoopy 1.2.4 (2008) HTTP client loadable from wp-includes despite _deprecated_file notice: unmaintained code shipped in core surface.
Weak hash for HMAC: wp_hash defaults to MD5 for hash_hmac: weak digest derives nonces, scheme salts and integrity tokens across core, eroding robustness over time.
Broken algorithm: wp_salt scheme salt via hash_hmac md5 $scheme $values key: broken hash primitive chosen when stronger hmac sha256 or sha384 are available.
Broken algorithm: wp_check_password backward-compat branch validates legacy md5 password: MD5 remains an accepted password verifier for old account hashes.
Weak PRNG: wp_generate_password fallback uses md5 uniqid microtime mt_rand seed: weak entropy reachable only on PHP without random_int but yields predictable secrets.
Missing SameSite: wp_set_auth_cookie setcookie positional args without SameSite attribute: auth and logged-in cookies lack cross-site request protection.
Weak PRNG: plugin editor scrape_key generated as md5 rand: rand is not a cryptographic PRNG, yielding predictable security-sensitive transient identifier.
Weak PRNG: plugin editor scrape_nonce generated as string rand: insecure PRNG output reused as anti-CSRF nonce for loopback fatal-error scrape probe.
Disabled TLS verification: spawn_cron loopback wp_remote_post sslverify false via https_local_ssl_verify default: certificate validation off on cron self-call.
Disabled TLS verification: HTTPS support fallback wp_remote_request sslverify false: certificate validation disabled during the secondary HTTPS probe path.
Cross-site scripting: trackback_response echoes error_message into XML message tag without escaping: wp_new_comment error text can carry input fragments.
Cross-site scripting: signup form echoes WP_Error blogname message into HTML without esc_html: secure-by-default violation if plugin reintroduces raw input.
Cross-site scripting: signup form echoes WP_Error blog_title message without esc_html: relies on upstream sanitization rather than output-time escaping.
Cross-site scripting: signup form echoes WP_Error user_name without esc_html: sink unsafe by default if filter or plugin reintroduces raw input into error text.
Cross-site scripting: signup form echoes WP_Error user_email without esc_html: email field error text is rendered unsanitized at the output boundary.
Cross-site scripting: signup form echoes WP_Error generic error without esc_html: generic error channel carries arbitrary plugin-supplied text into rendered HTML.
Account enumeration: wp_authenticate_username_password returns distinct invalid_username and incorrect_password WP_Error codes: reveals whether a username exists.
Insecure deserialization: maybe_unserialize invokes @unserialize trim data on stored option and meta values: attacker-written payload enables PHP object injection.
Information exposure: wp_generator emits WordPress version in the generator meta tag: aids fingerprinting and targeted version-specific exploit selection.
Permissive CORS: get_allowed_http_origins permits both http and https variants of admin and home host: weakens cross-origin policy on HTTPS-only sites.
Weak PRNG: PHPass random pool fallback builds entropy via md5 microtime random_state: cryptographically weak when /dev/urandom and openssl are unavailable.
XXE: DOMDocument loadXML consumes oEmbed XML response with no LIBXML_NONET option set: doctype is checked after parsing, allowing entity processing on older PHP defaults.
